articles.title: Apple II Forever!
articles.description: Apple would never have survived a decade without Steve Wozniak’s marvelous machine.

articles.title: For $200 more, you can get a MacBook Air
articles.description: The article explains how spending an extra $200 can get you a newer MacBook Air. It outlines the upgrades and why the price bump may be worth it.

articles.title: Steve Jobs and the greatest run of products in tech history
articles.description: The article examines Steve Jobs' string of iconic products—from the iMac and iBook to the iPod—that defined an era of innovation in tech. It argues this period represents the greatest run of products in technology history.

articles.title: These retractable studded tires might save our roads, ears, and lungs
articles.description: Nokian's new retractable studded tires aim to improve winter driving by reducing road noise and particle emissions while still providing the grip needed for icy conditions.

articles.title: Rank the 50 best Apple products
articles.description: The Verge invites readers to vote on the 50 best Apple products, spotlighting the company's most iconic devices and innovations. Share your picks and see how your favorites rank against the rest.

articles.title: There is no ethical consumption of HBO’s Harry Potter series
articles.description: The article argues that watching HBO's upcoming Harry Potter series raises ethical concerns, questioning whether audiences can support the project given the surrounding controversies.

articles.title: its iOS 26.4 betas
articles.description: Apple started testing encrypted RCS messaging with its iOS 26.4 betas, noting the feature would arrive in a future update. The first iOS 26.5 developer beta now includes encrypted RCS, suggesting a public launch may be imminent.

articles.title: 150 million users later, Roblox competitor Rec Room is shutting down
articles.description: Online multiplayer platform Rec Room, once hailed as a major competitor to Roblox and boasting 150 million users, announced it will shut down. The closure marks the end of the social‑gaming service after years of growth.

articles.title: Here are our favorite spring cleaning deals from Amazon’s Big Spring Sale
articles.description: The Verge highlights top spring cleaning gadgets—including vacuums, tools, and air purifiers—available at discounted prices during Amazon’s Big Spring Sale.

articles.title: The origin story of Apple’s long-running relationship with Foxconn
articles.description: An excerpt from Patrick McGee’s Apple in China.

articles.title: Apple @ 50
articles.description: Apple celebrates its 50th anniversary, looking back at the company's evolution and impact on technology.

articles.title: Eidos Montreal is laying off 124 employees
articles.description: The Embracer-owned studio behind Marvel’s Guardians of the Galaxy and Deus Ex: Mankind Divided announced it is laying off 124 employees, citing changing project needs across production and support teams. Studio head David Anfossi is also departing.

articles.title: Bambu Lab Settles with Pop Mart Over 3D Print File Takedown
articles.description: Bambu Lab reached a settlement with Pop Mart over the unauthorized distribution of 3D‑print files, just before a Chinese courtroom would have forced it to defend the hosting of those files. The company removed the files, issued a public apology, and the case suggests other IP rights holders may increase pressure on the 3D‑printing community.

articles.title: Android Auto Google amps EV charging routes
articles.description: “We’re bringing Maps’ AI-powered EV charging features to over 350 car models with Android Auto,” the company writes. It should predict where, when, and how long you’ll need to charge — after you punch in charge level manually. Google doesn’t mention battery preconditioning, though both Apple and Google are pursuing that vehicle‑by‑vehicle.

articles.title: like Alibaba
articles.description: After users in China reported seeing Apple Intelligence on their iPhones, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said these AI-powered features launched in “error” and Apple has since taken them offline. The Chinese government now requires Apple to partner with local companies like Alibaba to power AI features in the country.

articles.title: Why OpenAI killed Sora
articles.description: Too much compute, too much competition, and skeptical investors.

articles.title: The first Apple Home Key-ready smart lock with UWB is cheaper during Amazon’s Big Spring Sale
articles.description: Aqara's U400 smart lock, the first to support Apple Home Key and Ultra‑Wideband (UWB), is now available at a reduced price as part of Amazon’s Big Spring Sale. The deal brings advanced home‑entry tech to a wider audience without breaking the bank.

articles.title: Apple’s Finder Guy Is So Dang Cute
articles.description: The little character inspired by the Finder logo has been briefly featured as part of Apple’s marketing for the MacBook Neo, but on Monday, the company uploaded three new videos to its TikTok account starring the mascot. I love it.

articles.title: KitchenAid redesigned its iconic mixer so you can set an exact speed
articles.description: KitchenAid has updated its classic Artisan stand mixer with a new speed‑control feature that lets users set precise RPMs, offering more accuracy for mixing tasks.

articles.title: Vivo launches X300 Ultra flagship ‘designed for professional photography’
articles.description: Vivo has unveiled its new X300 Ultra flagship smartphone, promoted as a device built specifically for professional photography, featuring advanced camera hardware and software.

articles.title: Uber increases stake in WeRide as robotaxi partnership ramps up in Dubai
articles.description: Uber has raised its investment in Chinese autonomous‑vehicle startup WeRide, expanding their robotaxi collaboration in Dubai.
articles.author: Kirsten Korosec

articles.title: Hacker hijacks Axios open-source project, used by millions, to push malware
articles.description: A security breach was discovered in the popular Axios open-source library, where a hacker injected malicious code that could affect millions of applications. The incident highlights the growing risk of supply‑chain attacks targeting widely used JavaScript tools.
articles.author: Lorenzo Franceschi-Bicchierai

articles.title: FedEx chooses partnerships over proprietary tech for its automation strategy
articles.description: FedEx is opting to work with external partners rather than develop its own technology to drive automation across its logistics network, aiming for faster innovation and cost efficiency.

articles.title: Nomadic raises $8.4 million to wrangle the data pouring off autonomous vehicles
articles.description: Nomadic, a startup focused on autonomous‑vehicle data management, secured $8.4 million in funding to build tools that can handle the massive streams of data generated by self‑driving cars.

articles.title: Health data giant CareCloud says hackers accessed patients’ medical records
articles.description: CareCloud, a leading electronic health record provider, confirmed that hackers breached its systems and accessed patients' medical records, highlighting growing cybersecurity risks in the healthcare sector.
articles.author: Zack Whittaker

articles.title: Rivian spinoff Also will build autonomous delivery vehicles for DoorDash

articles.description: Airbnb is rolling out a private car pick‑up service that allows guests to schedule rides directly through the platform, streamlining travel to and from listings. The move expands Airbnb’s travel ecosystem beyond lodging.
